prompt: An exponential function $f$ satisfies $f(1) = 6$, $f(2) = 18$, and $f(3) = 54$. What is the value of $f(0)$?
hint: An exponential function multiplies by the same number at every step. Use the given outputs to find that multiplier.

hints.text: An exponential function multiplies by the same number at every step. Use the given outputs to find that multiplier.
Since $18 \div 6 = 3$ and $54 \div 18 = 3$, each step forward multiplies by $3$. Going from $f(1)$ back to $f(0)$ does the opposite.
Stepping back one place divides by $3$, so $f(0) = 6 \div 3 = 2$.

learningObjective: Extend an exponential pattern backwards to its initial value.
explanation: Consecutive outputs have the same ratio, $\dfrac{18}{6} = \dfrac{54}{18} = 3$, which is what makes the function exponential.
Moving forward one step multiplies by $3$, so moving backward one step divides by $3$.
Apply that to the first known value: $f(0) = \dfrac{6}{3} = 2$, so the value of $f(0)$ is $2$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Linear or exponential? Check differences and ratios
steps: Differences here are $12$ and $36$ — not constant, so the function is not linear.
Ratios are $3$ and $3$ — constant, so it is exponential.
Running both checks takes ten seconds and settles every "which model fits this table" question on the test.
